title: Notice communication
body: Watch one familiar routine. Notice pointing, movement, pictures or words. Respond without asking for a performance.

steps.title: Join something she enjoys
steps.body: Bring a familiar book, drawing materials or another activity she already likes.

demo.caption: Sit nearby and let her choose whether to join.
demo.accept: She may join, watch, move away or say no.

demo.caption: Follow what interests her. Describe one thing without asking a question.
demo.accept: A look, movement, gesture, picture or word can be communication.

demo.caption: Pause and respond to her message. If she wants to stop, stop.
demo.accept: No spoken answer or eye contact is needed.

steps.title: Offer two real choices
steps.body: Use two familiar things that are available now, such as a book and a ball.

demo.caption: Place both options where she can see and reach them comfortably.
demo.accept: Neither is also a valid choice.

demo.caption: Give her quiet time. Notice which item she looks toward, reaches for or indicates.
demo.say: You can stay quiet while she decides.
demo.accept: If the meaning is unclear, offer the choices again without testing.

demo.caption: Offer the item she indicates and share the activity if she wants.
demo.accept: She may change her mind. Do not require a word or a tap.

steps.title: Show how to ask for a break
steps.body: Keep the break picture nearby during an optional activity.

demo.caption: Point to the break picture while saying its meaning naturally.
demo.accept: She does not need to copy you.

demo.caption: Pause the activity when she signals discomfort, no or stop.
demo.accept: Respond to her message even if she does not use the picture.

demo.caption: Offer rest and finish for today if she wants. Keep the picture board available.
demo.accept: Water, food, comfort and rest never depend on a response.

title: Offer a real choice
body: Show two available, preferred activities. Accept a look, gesture, picture or word; either choice is valid.

title: Model a picture
body: Point to one relevant picture while speaking naturally. Leave the board within reach; imitation is optional.

title: Respect no and stop
body: Show how to indicate no or stop during an optional activity. Honour refusal and offer a pause.

title: Make help accessible
body: Model help in a naturally occurring moment. Give help promptly; do not create frustration to obtain a request.

title: Share an interest
body: Join an activity she chooses. Comment briefly and allow quiet time. No eye contact or spoken answer is required.

title: Review and rest
body: Notice which supports felt comfortable this week. Repeat a favourite moment or take a rest day.

title: Support a familiar routine
body: Choose one manageable part of handwashing or dressing. Show the step and offer the help she wants.

title: Offer a break
body: Keep the break picture visible. Offer a quieter space or pause when she communicates discomfort.

title: Communicate discomfort
body: Show the pain and help pictures without testing her. Respond to discomfort; new or severe symptoms need medical attention.

title: Keep pictures nearby
body: Carry a printed board into a familiar setting. Keep her usual ways of communicating available too.

title: Share with another caregiver
body: With family permission, show another trusted adult how to model pictures and respect refusal.

title: Support privacy and choice
body: Use age-respectful language during self-care. Explain before helping, respect privacy and offer choices.

title: Choose what to repeat
body: Review her preferences and your observations. Keep useful supports; change uncomfortable ones with professional input where available.
